questions.question: Q1. What is the total duration of the evaluation countdown timer before the final report modal triggers?

explanations.a: Incorrect. The countdown is longer than 30 seconds.
explanations.b: Correct. The simulation starts with a standalone center timer panel set exactly to 45.00s.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The timer is calibrated to 45 seconds, not 60.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The session runs for 45 seconds before freezing physics.

questions.question: Q2. Which visual feedback directly represents active tire smoke particles during an unvectored spinout?

answers.a: Bright green neon lines ahead of the chassis
answers.c: Warm cocoa smoke dust expanding and fading away
answers.d: Solid black grid blocks on the ground plane

explanations.a: Incorrect. Green lines represent the vehicle's predictive trajectory pathway.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Flashing red tail lamps represent a critical slip state or warning overlay, not particle generation.
explanations.c: Correct. The canvas renders a warm cocoa dust particle effect (`rgba(229, 220, 214, ...)`) that dynamically expands in size and fades in alpha opacity during active unvectored slipping.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The grid lines are light slate gray and remain stationary relative to world coordinates.

questions.question: Q3. What is the default base motor torque value when initializing or resetting the simulation?

explanations.a: Incorrect. 75 Nm is the nominal split torque delivered to an individual wheel when the base torque is at its default setting.
explanations.b: Correct. The range slider initializes at a default base motor torque of 150 Nm.
explanations.c: Incorrect. 300 Nm is within the adjustable range but is not the default value.
explanations.d: Incorrect. 400 Nm is the maximum upper limit of the torque range slider.

questions.question: Q4. In Scenario B (Power Slide Cornering), what are the locked programmatic values for torque and steering?

explanations.a: Incorrect. These are the fixed operational configurations for Scenario A (Black Ice Curve).
explanations.b: Incorrect. These are the standard sandbox default values.
explanations.c: Correct. Scenario B locks the surface friction to 0.80, applies max torque at 400 Nm, and locks steering at a hard right turning lock of 45°.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The programmatic lock forces positive steering angle values (+45°), not negative values.

questions.question: Q5. What color layout does an individual card background transition to when highlighted by an active engineering scenario?

answers.a: Gourmet cream with a soft cocoa border
answers.b: Dark cocoa chocolate background with high-contrast cream text
answers.c: Pistachio green with glowing neon edges

explanations.a: Incorrect. This is the default style of a standard HUD card before any active selection scenario highlight is triggered.
explanations.b: Correct. Selecting an engineering scenario activates the `.active-highlight` stylesheet rules, which swap the card background to the primary dark chocolate text color (`#2d1a12`) and force all internal typography into high-contrast cream (`#fbf8f3`).
explanations.c: Incorrect. Green is used for nominal stability statuses, not the background card highlight.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The radial gradient is applied strictly to the canvas ground background layout.

questions.question: Q6. What effective tire rolling radius ($r$) is utilized by the physics system to convert motor torque to linear traction demand force?

explanations.a: Incorrect. The code defines a larger value for the physics loop calculations.
explanations.b: Correct. The constant `TIRE_RADIUS` is hardcoded directly to 0.3 meters inside the calculation engine.
explanations.d: Incorrect. 1.00 meter is the upper bounds configuration limit for friction coefficient values, not tire dimension.

questions.question: Q7. Where on the simulation layout screen are the dynamic Force Balance Limit Bars visualized?

answers.b: Directly above the bottom horizontal control sliders
answers.c: Inside the left column's Proving Ground Logs card
answers.d: Floating directly behind the 3D wheels on the canvas

explanations.a: Incorrect. The right-side cards render mathematical equations and alphanumeric data, not graphical balance tracks.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The bottom area houses input controls and numeric torque readouts.
explanations.c: Correct. The script systematically injects the left and right rear wheel grip limit tracks directly into the `observationsBox` inner HTML inside the left column.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The canvas displays friction ellipses and vectors, but the horizontal fill bars are kept inside the HUD panel structure.

questions.question: Q8. If the evaluation report reflects that Torque Vectoring was active for less than 30% of the duration, what physical verdict is generated?

answers.c: Car Spun Out due to 50:50 Split

explanations.a: Incorrect. This text requires active vectoring tracking metrics greater than 70% accompanied by minimal slip indicators.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This is the fallback message when the data sits between the extreme assessment evaluation boundaries.
explanations.c: Correct. Under 30% vectoring utilization triggers the summary explaining that weight transfer starved the inner tire due to a rigid 50:50 power split under load transfer.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This is an imaginary error type; the system handles slip cases deterministically without hard throwing errors.

questions.question: Q9. What happens to the user input sliders when Scenario A or Scenario B is actively running?

answers.a: They are completely hidden from the viewport display area
answers.b: They scale up in size to permit precise fine-tuning adjustments
answers.c: They are programmatically locked and styled with reduced opacity
answers.d: They modify vehicle parameters but lock out the master vectoring toggle

explanations.a: Incorrect. The controllers stay fully visible to let students read the active locked configurations.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The physical dimensions do not expand.
explanations.c: Correct. Preset engineering scenarios drop a `.disabled` utility class onto the elements, restricting mouse interaction events via pointer styling and dimming visual visibility to 42% opacity.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Both the input ranges and the vectoring switch are mutually locked out during a preset test run.

questions.question: Q10. How does the predictive path arrow change visually on the canvas when the vehicle state is slipping without torque vectoring?

answers.a: It remains a thin, static blue line pointing along the steering vector
answers.b: It expands in thickness and flashes dynamically between soft and dark red
answers.c: It morphs into an interconnected series of yellow arrows pointing sideways
answers.d: It disappears completely from the ground grid view plane

explanations.a: Incorrect. The line is thick, active, and color-coded based on traction mechanics.
explanations.b: Correct. Under high slip without torque vectoring optimization, the predictive pathway color loops through a temporal check to flash between `#f87171` and `#dc2626` while its blur shadow thickness expands to 12.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Sideways arrows are vector representations rendered at the contact patches, not the path trail trajectory.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The pathway stays fully visible to illustrate the loss of structural direction.
